One adstock step per channel

Source: R/steps-helpers.R
step_adstock_channels.Rd

Adds one step_adstock() per media column, so that each channel gets its own decay, or its own tuning parameter. A single step applies one set of kernel parameters to every column it selects, and channels rarely share a carryover: mm_weekly was simulated with a decay of 0.85 for television and 0.15 for search.

Usage

step_adstock_channels(recipe, channels, ...)

Arguments

recipe

A recipe object.

channels

Character vector naming the media columns, one step each.

...

Named arguments for step_adstock(), such as index, by, decay and kernel, applied to every channel. The kernel parameters decay, max_lag, shape, scale and peak also take one value per channel, as a vector or list named by channel: decay = c(tv = 0.85, search = 0.15). Marking one of them with tune() gives each channel a tuning parameter of its own, with the ids decay_tv, decay_search and so on; tune("carry") gives carry_tv. A tune() without an id inside a list named by channel gets the same form of id.

Value

recipe with one step_adstock() added per channel, in the order of channels.

Details

Each step selects its channel with all_of() and the channel's name as a string, fixed when the step is added. A loop that writes all_of(ch) selects the last channel in every step instead, since selectors are evaluated at prep(), after the loop has finished. Step ids start with adstock_ and the channel's name, so tidy() on the recipe shows which step is which.

With tune(), hardhat::extract_parameter_set_dials() lists one parameter per channel, and tune::tune_grid() and tune::tune_bayes() search them together with the rest of the workflow's parameters.

See also

step_adstock() for the arguments, carryover_decay() for the tuning ranges.

Examples

library(recipes)
data(mm_weekly)

# A fixed decay for each channel
rec <- recipe(revenue ~ ., data = mm_weekly) |>
  step_adstock_channels(c("tv", "search"), index = "date", by = "geo",
                        decay = c(tv = 0.85, search = 0.15)) |>
  prep()
tidy(rec)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 6
#>   number operation type    trained skip  id                  
#>    <int> <chr>     <chr>   <lgl>   <lgl> <chr>               
#> 1      1 step      adstock TRUE    FALSE adstock_tv_vYRsf    
#> 2      2 step      adstock TRUE    FALSE adstock_search_RyDPM
tidy(rec, number = 2)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 13
#>   terms  group   kernel    decay max_lag shape scale type   peak start state
#>   <chr>  <chr>   <chr>     <dbl>   <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <chr> <dbl> <chr> <dbl>
#> 1 search north   geometric  0.15     Inf    NA    NA NA       NA zero   592.
#> 2 search central geometric  0.15     Inf    NA    NA NA       NA zero   368.
#> 3 search south   geometric  0.15     Inf    NA    NA NA       NA zero   769.
#> # ℹ 2 more variables: state_length <int>, id <chr>

# One tuning parameter per channel
tuned <- recipe(revenue ~ ., data = mm_weekly) |>
  step_adstock_channels(c("tv", "search"), index = "date", by = "geo",
                        decay = hardhat::tune())
hardhat::extract_parameter_set_dials(tuned)
#> Collection of 2 parameters for tuning
#> 
#>    identifier  type    object
#>      decay_tv decay nparam[+]
#>  decay_search decay nparam[+]
#>
